answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy is mostly an economics problem. Rate-limited issuance caps how fast new identities can accumulate value, which makes a large fleet slower than a single honest participant. Think of it as a basalt the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single shale of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a delta of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. Cost per identity is the whole lever; everything else is decoration.
